facts.label: Comparativos paralelos
facts.sub: The more you practise, the better you get. The earlier we start, the easier it is. Duas mudanças ligadas, com the em cada parte.

facts.label: Quanto mais…, melhor…
facts.sub: Use the + comparativo, the + comparativo para dizer que duas mudanças andam juntas: The more you practise, the better you get. A primeira parte é a causa e a segunda é o resultado.

facts.label: Com adjetivos
facts.sub: Use o comparativo do adjetivo: The earlier we start, the easier it becomes. Adjetivos curtos recebem -er (earlier, easier). Adjetivos longos usam more: the more confident I am, the more I speak.

pages.title: Practice makes progress in Liverpool · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a windy Thursday evening in Liverpool. Carla and Camila sit in an English classroom. The lesson has just finished, but they stay. They both want to speak with more confidence. A big exam is only two months away. They share ideas for studying better.

“Camila, the more I practise my pronunciation, the more confident I feel in class.” says Carla. “That is true for me too. The harder I study, the faster my vocabulary grows.” says Camila. “Our teacher says the more we repeat, the longer we remember new words.” says Carla.
